To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) clay minerals catalyze the formation of RNA oligomers, (ii) peptides catalyze the RNA polymerization reaction, (iii) clay minerals, peptides and lipids cooperate to form RNA oligomers and (iv) the resulting RNAs and peptides might have mutualistically catalyzed the formation of each other, leading to the first functional RNAs and catalysts.
the RNA polymerization is catalyzed by clays, peptides catalyze the formation of the RNA precursors, and the resulting RNAs catalyze the synthesis of the peptides.

clay minerals and peptides can catalyze non-enzymatically the formation of RNA oligomers, and that the combination of these two models can lead to an RNA-peptide system that might have preceded the RNA world.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the origin of the first RNAs, which might have been catalytically synthesized in a multi-component prebiotical system and subsequently have been involved in a mutualistic cooperation with peptides, which might have catalyzed the formation of the latter.
the emergence and evolution of the first functional RNAs and proteins in a prebiotic soup containing clay, lipids, peptides, and RNA.
the emergence of RNA, a key step in the origin of life, and the role of clay minerals, lipids, and peptides in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the origin of life is still an enigma, which will be solved only by the discovery of new prebiotic reactions, and the development of new experimental approaches.
the emergence of the first functional RNA polymers was a synergistic and mutualistic process, which might be a general principle for the emergence of life.
the RNA polymerization and self-replication are still a mystery and that the RNA world is still far away.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the emergence of life was a complex process, which required the cooperation between the building blocks of life and their mutualism, in order to reach functional RNA and peptides.

the RNA world is a complex, multi-component system in which all the building blocks cooperate in a synergistic way, leading towards a more evolved system, in which mutualistic cooperation between RNA and peptides would be the key for life’s origin.
non-enzymatically synthesized RNA oligomers are not just a curiosity but rather a key component in the emergence and evolution of the first life on Earth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to understand how the first polymers were formed, it is necessary to consider the interplay between different components in a complex prebiotic soup.
, in order for the RNA world hypothesis to be plausible, the RNA polymerization process must have been catalyze by a complex system involving more than one component.
, despite the complexity of the prebiotic environment, a synergistic approach might be the most efficient way to study the emergence of the RNA world and its subsequent evolution.
